druid-lake.name: Druid Lake
druid-lake.description: Druid Lake is the park's reservoir landscape and the focus of a reopened walking and rolling loop; it is scenery and recreation space, not a swimming lake.
druid-lake.address: 900 Druid Park Lake Drive, Baltimore, MD 21217
druid-lake.sourceLabel: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
druid-lake.location: Use the lake-loop access along Druid Park Lake Drive rather than the park's general pin. The modified continuous loop reopened in May 2025 after the underground tank project; fencing and signed restoration areas still control where visitors may go.
druid-lake.parking: Legal curb and park parking varies around the lake. Do not stop in the Big Jump lane or against construction barriers, and follow temporary event, restoration, and street-parking signs.
druid-lake.hours: Use the lake loop during ordinary daylight park hours. Construction, major events, storms, ice, maintenance, and temporary safety work can close or redirect parts of the route independently.
druid-lake.restrooms: There is no dependable restroom directly on the lake loop. Plan around staffed destinations such as Rawlings Conservatory or the Maryland Zoo during their own open hours, and do not assume those facilities admit non-ticketed restroom visits.
druid-lake.fees: Walking and rolling around Druid Lake is free. Nearby staffed attractions, programs, parking restrictions, and reserved events are separate.
druid-lake.accessibility: The reopened loop is paved, but temporary fencing, crossings, grades, construction transitions, and the park's surrounding high-speed roads can affect a step-free trip. Use current signs and the protected Big Jump connection where it serves the route.
druid-lake.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor park routes. Keep them out of the lake and restoration areas, yield on the shared path, and remove waste.
druid-lake.family: The loop is a practical stroller, walking, and bicycling objective when weather and construction are calm. Keep children beside an adult at road crossings and barriers, and do not treat the lake edge as a swimming or play-water area.
druid-lake.need: The loop is open, but the landscape has changed from its pre-construction form. Follow current fencing rather than old maps, and check Baltimore City notices before a trip built around uninterrupted access.

howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.name: Howard Peters Rawlings Conservatory
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.description: The historic glasshouse and five greenhouse environments are a separately staffed destination inside Druid Hill Park with much shorter hours than the surrounding grounds.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.location: Enter Druid Hill Park from Gwynns Falls Parkway, turn right after entering, and follow signs to 3100 Swann Drive. The conservatory is near McCulloh Street and Gwynns Falls Parkway, not beside the zoo entrance.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.parking: The conservatory documents ample free parking nearby inside Druid Hill Park. Vehicle access can be suspended for major events, so read the same-day notice before driving into the park.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.hours: Open Wednesday-Friday 11 a.m.-3 p.m. and Saturday-Sunday 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; closed Monday, Tuesday, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. The official visit page also lists full vehicle closure for AFRAM June 19-21, 2026 and a conservatory closure for the Caribbean Fest parade July 11, 2026.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.restrooms: Use the conservatory's visitor facilities during staffed hours. Do not rely on building access before opening, after closing, or during an event closure.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.fees: The official visit page offers advance donation and ticket options. Check the current ticket page rather than relying on an older admission amount.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.accessibility: Use the nearby parking and main visitor entrance for the shortest paved approach. Historic greenhouse aisles and event layouts can vary; contact the conservatory for a specific accommodation or group need.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.dogs: Pets are not a normal fit inside the conservatory. Qualified service animals should be confirmed under current visitor rules; ordinary park dog rules resume outside the staffed facility.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.family: The compact greenhouse environments work well as a weather-aware family stop, but adults should confirm the limited open days and supervise children around plants, glass, water, and narrow visitor aisles.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.need: Do not plan around general park hours. The conservatory is closed Monday and Tuesday, keeps short daytime hours, and posts event-related vehicle and building closures separately.

maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.name: Maryland Zoo in Baltimore
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.description: The Maryland Zoo is a ticketed, separately operated outdoor attraction within Druid Hill Park, with its own gate, parking, rules, food, restrooms, and daily operating schedule.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.location: Navigate to One Safari Place and the Maryland Zoo front gate, not the Druid Hill Park or Rawlings Conservatory pin. Use the zoo's current map after entering because exhibits and animal visibility can change during the day.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.parking: Use zoo-designated parking at the front-gate arrival. Free accessible spaces are to the left of the front gate on a first-come basis; event traffic elsewhere in Druid Hill Park can alter the approach.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.hours: The zoo publishes daily hours and alerts on its own site; the page checked August 10, 2026 showed 10 a.m.-4 p.m. Confirm the selected date because seasonal hours, events, weather, and animal operations can differ.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.restrooms: Accessible restrooms with baby-changing stations are distributed through the zoo. Family restrooms are documented near Whistle Stop Grille and inside the Penguin Education Center.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.fees: Zoo admission is ticketed and separate from free general park access. Use the official ticket page for current date-based admission, memberships, rentals, and paid experiences.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.accessibility: The zoo provides first-come accessible parking, accessible restrooms, ADA-compliant shuttles, and first-come wheelchair, ECV, and stroller rentals. Druid Hill topography and some animal areas create route or device limitations, so review the current accessibility page.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.dogs: Pets are not permitted anywhere on zoo grounds, including parking lots. ADA-defined service animals are permitted under the zoo's service-animal rules.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.family: The zoo is designed for family visits, but adults must supervise children, stay on marked paths, respect barriers, and accept that animals may choose off-exhibit areas.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.need: This is an outdoor, ticketed visit: the zoo says rain checks and refunds are not issued. Check weather, daily alerts, tickets, and the day's schedule before crossing the park.

chinese-pavilion.name: Chinese Pavilion
chinese-pavilion.description: The Chinese Pavilion is a distinctive open-air landmark on Swann Drive, useful as a precise meeting point and a short historic-landscape stop within the much larger park.
chinese-pavilion.address: Swann Drive, Druid Hill Park, Baltimore, MD 21217
chinese-pavilion.sourceLabel: Baltimore City Recreation and Parks master plan
chinese-pavilion.location: Use the geotagged pavilion point on Swann Drive. It is south of the conservatory and lake-side attractions, so the general Druid Hill Park pin is not a reliable walking destination.
chinese-pavilion.parking: Use an open legal park space serving Swann Drive and walk the final approach. Do not park on grass, block the pavilion, or assume a nearby event or maintenance lane is visitor parking.
chinese-pavilion.hours: The open-air pavilion follows ordinary daylight park access unless a permit, event, maintenance project, or posted closure controls the area.
chinese-pavilion.restrooms: There is no documented dependable restroom at the pavilion. Use a staffed destination during its own operating hours before walking to this landmark.
chinese-pavilion.fees: Casual outdoor viewing is free. Reserved or organized use may require a city permit.
chinese-pavilion.accessibility: The pavilion is beside a park drive and lawn setting, but curb, grade, surface, and event conditions vary. Review the final approach on arrival rather than assuming every side is step-free.
chinese-pavilion.dogs: Leashed dogs may accompany visitors in ordinary outdoor park space. Keep them out of permitted gatherings and remove waste.
chinese-pavilion.family: This is a short visual landmark rather than a staffed attraction. Children should stay with an adult around the road, steps, railings, and any event setup.
chinese-pavilion.need: There is no admission desk or guaranteed facility service here. Treat it as an outdoor landmark and pair it with another destination only after checking walking distance and current park access.

mansion-house-lawn.name: Mansion House Lawn
mansion-house-lawn.description: Mansion House Lawn is a broad historic open landscape near the zoo side of Druid Hill Park, suited to walking, informal recreation, and understanding the scale of the original estate grounds.
mansion-house-lawn.address: Mansion House Drive, Druid Hill Park, Baltimore, MD 21217
mansion-house-lawn.sourceLabel: Baltimore City Recreation and Parks master plan
mansion-house-lawn.location: Navigate to the mapped lawn on Mansion House Drive rather than to Druid Lake or Rawlings Conservatory. The photographed lawn is an open landscape, not the zoo's ticket entrance.
mansion-house-lawn.parking: Use a legal open space serving Mansion House Drive or the selected nearby attraction. Zoo parking and access rules apply if the trip enters zoo property; do not cross a closed gate or use service roads as shortcuts.
mansion-house-lawn.hours: The outdoor lawn follows daylight park access unless an event permit, zoo operation, maintenance activity, or posted closure restricts it.
mansion-house-lawn.restrooms: There is no guaranteed restroom on the lawn. Nearby zoo restrooms are inside the ticketed attraction, so plan restroom access before settling into this area.
mansion-house-lawn.fees: Casual access to ordinary park lawn is free. Zoo admission, permitted events, programs, and reservations are separate.
mansion-house-lawn.accessibility: Roadside and paved approaches exist, while the lawn itself is grass with natural grades and weather-sensitive footing. Use the nearest legal arrival point for a shorter firm-surface approach.
mansion-house-lawn.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor park areas but may not enter Maryland Zoo grounds. Keep dogs clear of organized activities and remove waste.
mansion-house-lawn.family: The open lawn offers room to pause and move, but it has no dedicated staffed family facilities. Maintain supervision near roads and confirm whether an event controls the space.
mansion-house-lawn.need: The lawn and zoo are adjacent but not interchangeable. A lawn visit does not include zoo entry, restrooms, or parking privileges, and permitted events can temporarily change access.

patterson-park-observatory.name: Patterson Park Observatory
patterson-park-observatory.description: The 1891-92 Observatory, widely called the Pagoda, is Patterson Park's signature hilltop landmark and viewpoint, but its interior is currently closed for maintenance indefinitely.
patterson-park-observatory.location: Use the mapped Observatory point near the west side of the park. Approach on park paths from the Baltimore Street, Pratt Street, or Patterson Park Avenue side rather than navigating to the pool on Linwood Avenue.
patterson-park-observatory.parking: There is no general visitor parking inside Patterson Park. Use legal perimeter street parking, read residential restrictions, and leave permitted and emergency vehicle routes clear.
patterson-park-observatory.hours: The exterior grounds follow dawn-to-dusk park hours. Although older schedules describe seasonal Sunday interior hours, the current landmarks page says the Observatory is closed for maintenance indefinitely; do not promise tower entry.
patterson-park-observatory.restrooms: There is no dependable public restroom inside the Observatory while it is closed. Plan around an open staffed park facility and verify access before walking uphill.
patterson-park-observatory.fees: Viewing the exterior and surrounding park is free. There is no current paid admission that overrides the indefinite interior closure.
patterson-park-observatory.accessibility: Paved park paths reach the hill area, but grades and the historic tower interior require separate consideration. The closed interior should not be treated as an available accessible viewpoint.
patterson-park-observatory.dogs: Leashed dogs may use surrounding park paths under the six-foot leash rule. Keep dogs outside the structure and away from gardens or posted event areas.
patterson-park-observatory.family: The exterior is a memorable family landmark and city-view stop, but adults should prepare children for a closed tower and supervise them on the hill, steps, and paths.
patterson-park-observatory.need: Current closure overrides the usual seasonal Sunday schedule. Visit for the exterior, gardens, and hilltop setting, and recheck the official landmarks page before expecting interior access.

boat-lake.name: Boat Lake
boat-lake.description: Boat Lake is Patterson Park's restored wetland and open-water habitat, now used for fishing, wildlife viewing, and education rather than public boating or swimming.
boat-lake.address: Patterson Park near Eastern Avenue and South Milton Avenue, Baltimore, MD 21224
boat-lake.location: The lake lies in the southern part of the park near Eastern Avenue and Milton Avenue. Use the mapped lake point and park paths; the Baltimore Street recreation-center address is on the opposite side of the park.
boat-lake.parking: Use legal perimeter street parking near Eastern Avenue or adjacent side streets, then walk in. Unauthorized private vehicles are not allowed on park paths.
boat-lake.hours: The outdoor lake area follows dawn-to-dusk park hours. Ice, storms, maintenance, habitat work, fishing restrictions, and events can change practical access.
boat-lake.restrooms: There is no dependable restroom at the shoreline. Use a staffed seasonal or recreation facility only when it is open, and plan for a walk across the park.
boat-lake.fees: Wildlife viewing and ordinary park access are free. Fishing rules and any required Maryland license still apply.
boat-lake.accessibility: Primary park approaches are paved, but shoreline edges, grass, wet surfaces, and habitat areas are not uniform. Stay on established paths and use the closest Eastern Avenue-side entrance.
boat-lake.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed at six feet or less outside the dog park. Keep dogs out of the water and wetland plantings and away from wildlife.
boat-lake.family: The lake is useful for birds, fish, and nature observation, but it is not a splash pad, swimming area, or boating attraction. Keep children beside an adult at the water edge.
boat-lake.need: The historic name can mislead visitors: current official guidance describes fishing, wildlife viewing, and education, not public boat rental or swimming.

marble-fountain.name: Marble Fountain
marble-fountain.description: The restored 1865 Marble Fountain is a small gathering landmark near the Lombard Street and Patterson Park Avenue side of the park.
marble-fountain.address: Patterson Park near East Lombard Street and South Patterson Park Avenue, Baltimore, MD 21231
marble-fountain.location: Use the destination's geotagged point near East Lombard Street and South Patterson Park Avenue. It is west of Boat Lake and far from the Linwood Avenue pool and rink.
marble-fountain.parking: Use legal perimeter street parking near Lombard Street or Patterson Park Avenue and walk in. Read neighborhood restrictions and do not drive onto park paths.
marble-fountain.hours: The outdoor fountain area follows dawn-to-dusk park hours. Water operation can be seasonal or interrupted by weather and maintenance, so the landmark may be visible without flowing.
marble-fountain.restrooms: There is no documented dependable restroom at the fountain. Verify an open staffed park facility before relying on restroom access.
marble-fountain.fees: Viewing the fountain is free. Permitted events held around it may control the immediate space.
marble-fountain.accessibility: The fountain is reached by paved park paths, while curb cuts, grades, temporary event barriers, and fountain-edge conditions can vary by approach.
marble-fountain.dogs: Leashed dogs may use surrounding paths under the six-foot leash rule. Keep them out of the basin and remove waste.
marble-fountain.family: The fountain makes a short visual stop, but the basin is not a splash pad. Children should remain outside the railing and with an adult.
marble-fountain.need: Do not make water flow the sole reason for the trip. Seasonal shutdown, maintenance, or an event can leave the fountain off or the immediate plaza occupied.

war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.name: War of 1812 Memorial Cannons
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.description: The memorial cannons sit beside the Observatory area and recall Patterson Park's role at Hampstead Hill during the defense of Baltimore.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.address: Patterson Park near the Observatory, Baltimore, MD 21224
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.location: Use the geotagged cannon point by the Observatory rather than searching the athletic-field or pool side of the park. The two landmarks can be visited in one short hilltop circuit.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.parking: Use legal perimeter street parking and walk to the Observatory hill. No general visitor vehicles are allowed on park paths.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.hours: The outdoor memorial follows dawn-to-dusk park access unless maintenance, a permitted event, or a posted closure controls the hilltop area.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.restrooms: There is no restroom at the cannons. The nearby Observatory interior is closed indefinitely and should not be counted as a restroom stop.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.fees: The outdoor memorial is free to view.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.accessibility: Paved park paths approach the hill, but grade and the immediate landscape should be assessed for the chosen mobility need. The cannons are historic objects, not play equipment.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.dogs: Leashed dogs may use surrounding paths under the six-foot leash rule. Keep animals off the memorial base and gardens.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.family: This is a compact history stop that pairs naturally with the Observatory exterior. Children should not climb or sit on the cannons and should stay with an adult on the hill.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.need: The site is unstaffed and has no interpretive desk or guaranteed facilities. Read the memorial in place, protect the historic objects, and plan restroom access elsewhere.

virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.name: Virginia S. Baker Recreation Center
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.description: Virginia S. Baker Recreation Center is Patterson Park's year-round indoor program hub, with a gym, multipurpose and meeting rooms, game room, kitchen, and computer lab.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.location: The center is inside the north side of the park near East Baltimore Street and Luzerne Avenue. Use 2601 East Baltimore Street rather than the southern pool, rink, or Boat Lake entrances.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.parking: Use legal perimeter street parking near Baltimore Street and walk to the center. There is no general visitor parking inside Patterson Park, and program or event demand can tighten nearby availability.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.hours: The center has year-round programming but does not share dawn-to-dusk park hours. Call 410-396-9156 or check the current city program schedule before expecting the building, gym, or a specific activity to be open.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.restrooms: Restroom access is tied to the recreation center being open for programs. Do not rely on indoor access outside current staffed hours.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.fees: Building entry and program costs vary by activity. Confirm the current city schedule, registration, age rules, and any fee before arriving.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.accessibility: Use the recreation-center entrance and exact city facility pin for the shortest approach. Contact the center for a program-specific accommodation or to confirm room and entrance access.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.dogs: Pets are not a normal fit inside the recreation center. ADA-defined service animals follow applicable facility rules; park leash rules apply outside.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.family: The center supports youth and adult programs year-round, but drop-in availability cannot be inferred from the park being open. Confirm the exact activity, age range, and registration first.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.need: This is a scheduled, staffed facility rather than an always-open park amenity. Call or check the current program listing before crossing the park for indoor access.
